raw: {"need": "Identity", "secondary": {"name": "Competence"}, "read": "A new hire on day one is in the middle of figuring out who they are in a professional context, what kind of worker they will be, and whether this place is somewhere they belong. Clear expectations feel like a gift or a threat depending entirely on how they land. If expectations come down as a list of rules, they read as a signal that the person is not trusted yet. The status angle is real: they want to walk in feeling like someone who is starting a career, not someone on probation.", "pull": {"collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Front-load every policy and standard on day one so nothing is ambiguous, which turns the first conversation into a compliance briefing and signals that following rules matters more than the person does."}, "mentorMove": "Set the standards clearly and early, but frame them as the conditions that let them do meaningful work and build a real reputation, not as the fence around acceptable behavior. Invite them into the why before you hand them the what.", "holdFirm": ["The standards themselves do not shift because someone is new.", "Expectations are named out loud, not left for them to guess."], "stayFlexible": ["How much they want to ask versus observe in the first week.", "Which parts of the role they want to dig into first as they get their footing."], "forceLevel": {"level": 1, "label": "Empathy"}, "script": [{"phase": "Connection", "words": "I am genuinely glad you are here. Starting a new job is one of those weeks where everything is coming at you at once, and I want you to know that feeling turned around for the first little while is completely normal, it does not mean anything about whether you belong here."}, {"phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Before I tell you anything about how we run things, I want to hear from you. What does a good first few months look like to you? What would make you feel like this was the right move?"}, {"phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I care about on my end. I want you doing work that matters and building a reputation you are proud of. Everything I am going to tell you about how we operate is in service of that, so if something does not make sense or feels like it is getting in the way, I want to know."}, {"phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am going to hold you to a high standard from the start, not because I am testing you, but because I think you can handle real work right away and I would rather treat you that way than ease you in so slowly the first month feels like a waste of your time."}], "longGame": "How you introduce expectations on day one sets the frame for every hard conversation after it. If they walk out Monday knowing you see them as a capable person whose growth you are invested in, they are far more likely to come to you when something is hard instead of quietly struggling or quietly checking out."}
situation: A new hire starts Monday and I want to set clear expectations.
